analysis.title: A $10 Billion Passive Bid Is Coming: Goldman Tracks SpaceX's Lockup Cliff Into The Index Funds
key_insights: Goldman's Ben Snider (US Weekly Kickstart) finds SpaceX has had little effect on index valuation. Removing it from the Nasdaq 100 lowers the index P/E only from 19.5x to 19.2x, because only 5% of SpaceX shares were tradable at IPO and index providers mostly ignored it.

About a third of SpaceX shares are now in the public float, up from 5% at IPO. Based on the lockup schedule, about half should be in the float by mid-2027, which Goldman says is consistent with historical large IPOs that had low initial floats.

Most US indices weight by free-float market cap, so SpaceX's weights should keep rising as lockups expire and each index rebalances. The Nasdaq 100 is the exception. Since a methodology change it weights companies with float below 33% at 3x their float market cap and switches to full listed market cap above 33%, so it has already front-run most of the float increase and the mechanical impact there should be relatively muted.
ETFs owned about $32B of SpaceX at the end of October (1.4% of market cap), up from $11B (0.5%) at the end of June. Roughly $20B of that sits in funds tracking the Nasdaq 100.

The largest pending passive demand is in the Russell 1000 Growth. SpaceX's weight would rise from 0.2% to 1.5% if the index were rebalanced today for the float already unlocked. With about $800B benchmarked to the index, that implies roughly $10.9B of passive buying. The next scheduled rebalance is December 11.

Other indices add much less if rebalanced today: $1.4B from the Nasdaq 100 and $0.5B each from the S&P Total Market and MSCI ACWI. The S&P 500, with $11.9T benchmarked, currently holds SpaceX at zero weight.

Ownership at the end of June, per Goldman estimates: insiders and stakeholders 68.8% ($1.56T), hedge funds 3.3%, mutual funds under 1%. The remaining 26.5% (about $600B) belongs to investors who do not report holdings, which Goldman says likely corresponds primarily to individual investors. Lockup schedules and the modest rise in passive ownership suggest insiders and individuals own the majority of shares today.
The article's framing is that the passive bid meets insiders whose shares are coming out of lockup. Mutual funds and hedge funds report September 30 holdings later this month.

Snider concludes SpaceX's impact on equity index performance, concentration and valuation has been much smaller than many investors expected. Nasdaq 100 sales growth falls about a point with SpaceX included, the return since inclusion is -10.3% vs -10.0% without it, and the top 10 stocks are 50% of the index either way. He compares it to Tesla's 2020 S&P 500 inclusion.

The S&P 500 has typically traded flat in the weeks around the five largest IPOs of the past 30 years (Visa, GM, Alibaba, Meta and SpaceX) before resuming its uptrend, and June followed that pattern. Snider cautions that the universe of comparable IPOs is small.

S&P 500 inclusion requires 12 months as a public company and positive GAAP net income for the latest quarter and the trailing four quarters combined. On consensus forecasts SpaceX meets the profit test once Q2 2027 results are out, pointing to inclusion in the second half of 2027. Snider notes a merger with a current S&P 500 constituent could be another route, reviewed case by case.
The article reports that with the small float, shorts piled in and the stock fell 20% below its IPO price, erasing $1.2T from its peak value, and SPCX's levered ETFs were down 65%.

SpaceX has raised capital repeatedly: $86B in the IPO, $25B of investment-grade bonds under two weeks later and, as of October, another $40B of chip-collateralized SPV debt via Apollo. The article expects December 11 to be the first real test of forced passive buying against insider supply.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman estimates over $10B of passive demand if the Russell 1000 Growth were rebalanced today for unlocked float, with the scheduled rebalance on December 11. Insider supply from lockup expiries is the offsetting factor.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 eligibility for SpaceX depends on positive GAAP net income for the latest quarter and the trailing four quarters combined. Consensus forecasts (an estimate, not a print) have SpaceX clearing that bar once Q2 2027 results are out.
risk_factors: Insider supply as lockups expire may absorb forced passive buying, since insiders and stakeholders held 68.8% of the company at the end of June.
The sample of comparable large IPOs is small, which limits the historical read on index and market behavior around the SpaceX listing.
SpaceX has raised large amounts of capital, including $86B in the IPO, $25B of IG bonds and $40B of chip-collateralized SPV debt via Apollo.
vol_and_positioning: Passive ETFs own about 1.4% of SpaceX ($32B) at the end of October vs 0.5% ($11B) at the end of June. Hedge funds held 3.3% and mutual funds under 1% at the end of June.
The article reports that shorts piled into SPCX while only 5% of the company was tradable, and that SPCX's levered ETFs were down 65% about a week after the stock fell 20% below its IPO price.
Forced passive buying from the December 11 Russell 1000 Growth rebalance is estimated at over $10B (about $10.9B), set against insider shares coming out of lockup.

tension_points.theme: SpaceX passive bid vs insider supply
tension_points.bull_case: Goldman estimates over $10B of additional passive demand from the Russell 1000 Growth rebalance on December 11, with more float and S&P 500 inclusion (second half of 2027) adding further index demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Insiders and stakeholders held 68.8% at the end of June and their shares are coming out of lockup, so forced passive buying meets people who have waited a year to sell. SpaceX has also raised large sums in debt and equity.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The December 11 Russell 1000 Growth rebalance is described as the first real test of whether passive demand or insider supply wins.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising float will force more passive buying, starting with the December 11 Russell 1000 Growth rebalance.
theme_stances.evidence: next scheduled rebalance of the Russell 1000 Growth Index is on December 11
